newsitem.title: GERMANY: German new car registrations seen up 2.4 pct in 97.
newsitem.headline: German new car registrations seen up 2.4 pct in 97.

text.p: The German Association of Motor Vehicle Importers (VDIK) said on Friday it expects total German car registrations this year to climb 2.4 percent to 3.58 million vehicles.
Speaking at a trade show, association chief Volker Lange said foreign car makers had increased their share of the German market by one and a half percentage points so far this year to 33 percent.

New car registrations in Germany between January and March of this year, he said, were down about five percent to 867,000 units. The figure was depressed, however, because there were two fewer working days in March this year than in March 1995.
Lange said that although consumers faced uncertainties about Bonn's economic and financial policies, they remained interested in buying new cars, which would boost to demand during the year.
